blocks.text: Design a live streaming platform like Twitch, letting a streamer broadcast video in real time to potentially hundreds of thousands of simultaneous viewers, each watching at whatever quality their own connection can actually sustain. This category's other video designs cover on-demand content, transcoded once, offline, with no urgency at all. A live stream flips that constraint entirely: every single segment of video must be transcoded to every quality level within a strict, ongoing latency budget, over and over, for as long as the stream continues, since a live moment that takes too long to reach viewers stops being live at all.

blocks.alt: Every captured live segment is transcoded to every quality level under a strict latency budget and distributed immediately, while each viewer's player continuously selects whichever quality its own current bandwidth can actually sustain

blocks.text: The two techniques that make this work are a real-time transcoding pipeline racing a strict per-segment latency budget, rather than the leisurely, one-time transcode an on-demand video affords, and adaptive bitrate selection, where each viewer's own player continuously measures its available bandwidth and picks the best quality rendition it can currently sustain, switching smoothly at the next segment boundary as conditions change.

blocks.text: A streamer should be able to broadcast live video, authenticated by a stream key, to an ingest server. The platform should transcode each captured segment into multiple quality levels in real time and make them available to viewers within a few seconds. A viewer's player should automatically select the best video quality its current bandwidth can sustain, adapting smoothly as conditions change. Viewers should be able to chat in real time alongside the live video.

blocks.alt: Genuinely low, real time latency, smooth and adaptive playback quality, massive concurrent live viewership, real time chat alongside video, and protected streamer identity

blocks.text: Genuinely low, real-time latency means a live moment has to reach viewers within a few seconds, nothing close to the minutes of processing delay that would be entirely acceptable for on-demand video. Smooth, adaptive playback quality means a viewer's connection quality changes constantly, and playback needs to adapt to that smoothly rather than stalling or buffering. Massive concurrent live viewership means a single popular stream can draw hundreds of thousands of simultaneous viewers all watching the exact same live moment together. Real-time chat alongside video means chat needs to feel genuinely synchronized with what is happening on screen, not a system operating apart from it. And protected streamer identity means a stolen stream key would let an attacker broadcast fraudulently as if they were someone else entirely.

class LiveTranscodePipeline:
    # Enforces a strict per-segment latency budget for live transcoding: a
    # segment finishing within budget is distributed on time, one that misses
    # it is dropped rather than allowed to delay the live stream further.
    def __init__(self, latency_budget_millis):
        self.latency_budget_millis = latency_budget_millis

    def process_segment(self, segment_id, captured_at, transcoding_completed_at):
        latency = transcoding_completed_at - captured_at
        if latency <= self.latency_budget_millis:
            return f"ON_TIME, latency={latency}ms, distributed immediately"
        else:
            return f"DROPPED, latency={latency}ms exceeds the {self.latency_budget_millis}ms budget"


class AdaptiveBitrateSelector:
    # Selects the highest quality rendition whose bitrate still comfortably
    # fits within a viewer's currently measured bandwidth, falling back to
    # the lowest available quality if even that does not fit, rather than
    # showing nothing at all.
    def __init__(self, quality_bitrates_kbps):
        self.quality_bitrates_kbps = quality_bitrates_kbps  # quality label -> required bitrate

    def select_quality(self, measured_bandwidth_kbps):
        best = None
        best_bitrate = -1
        lowest_quality = None
        lowest_bitrate = float('inf')

        for quality, bitrate in self.quality_bitrates_kbps.items():
            if bitrate < lowest_bitrate:
                lowest_bitrate = bitrate
                lowest_quality = quality  # track the lowest quality as a fallback
            if bitrate <= measured_bandwidth_kbps and bitrate > best_bitrate:
                best_bitrate = bitrate
                best = quality  # the highest quality that still comfortably fits

        return best if best is not None else lowest_quality  # fall back to the lowest quality rather than nothing at all


def main():
    pipeline = LiveTranscodePipeline(4000)  # 4 second latency budget

    # Segment 1: captured at t=1000, finishes transcoding at t=3500 (2500ms latency): within budget.
    print("Segment 1:", pipeline.process_segment("seg-1", 1000, 3500))

    # Segment 2: captured at t=1000, finishes transcoding at t=6000 (5000ms latency): exceeds budget.
    print("Segment 2:", pipeline.process_segment("seg-2", 1000, 6000))

    # Adaptive bitrate selection.
    qualities = {"1080p": 6000, "720p": 3000, "480p": 1500, "360p": 800}
    selector = AdaptiveBitrateSelector(qualities)

    print("Viewer with 5000 kbps selects:", selector.select_quality(5000))
    print("Viewer with 7000 kbps selects:", selector.select_quality(7000))
    print("Viewer with 500 kbps (very poor connection) selects:", selector.select_quality(500))

    print("Same viewer, bandwidth drops to 1000 kbps, next segment selects:", selector.select_quality(1000))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
